newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end off as market awaits fuel hike.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end off as market awaits fuel hike.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange slipped back from record levels in moderate trade as the market awaited signs the government would go ahead with a gasoline price increase Thursday as planned, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index fell 0.36 percent to 9,681.53, as 20 stocks fell, 12 rose and 11 closed flat.
Dealers said the market, which had risen strongly to record closes during the last two sessions, opened firm, but fell back as interest waned.
"There are a few things in the air which could have repercussions for the market such as the gasoline price," one broker said.
Gasoline price rises are sensitive political issues in Venezuela and the government recently delayed the 27 percent rise to give private sector companies time to adjust wages.

By sticking to its July 31 date for rising prices, the government would reaffirm its commitment to reform and boost confidence of foreign investors who have been more wary in recent days, brokers said.

Among leading stocks, benchmark Electricidad de Caracas closed unchanged at 830.00 bolivars, telephone company CANTV fell 38.00 bolivars to 3,111.00 bolivars and medium sized bank Banco Union dropped 400.00 bolivars to 1,800 bolivars.
An ownership battle for Banco Union has seen the stock's price jump in recent sessions and a bout of profit-taking was to be expected, brokers said.
Total trade was 7.023 billion bolivars ($14.2 million).
